Prove it: native datastream suite: a 250 ms 32-segment bundle accepted at horizon 250, refused past it, samples still capped at 20 ms; clients/js test decodes both keys from a fixture GRANT; MFP plugin's hand-tuned sync offset (RFC-014 shape) can be deleted against the advertised value.

title: Node graph: author hub relationships and client-side mappings (Intiface apps to machine, machine state to toys) with one map vocabulary
description: Operator direction 2026-10-01 (RFC-078 ruling): a node-like editor in Phosphor. Two evaluation homes, one vocabulary. (1) HUB relationships (RFC-078): source field, map node, target accessory field; authored here, stored on the hub through the relationships STORE (RFC-067 action.store verbs), evaluated on the hub with no session present; the editor reads the store and roster and shows armed/faulted state. (2) CLIENT-side mappings that cannot live on the hub because one end is connected to Phosphor, not the hub: an Intiface app that only sends vibrate or rotate driving the machine (map to stroke speed, depth or a pattern parameter through the intent path, Prime Rule: one session), machine state (position, speed, safety) driving a buttplug toy's outputs, Intiface input or sensors driving either. Same seven map nodes as RFC-078's relationship_maps (linear_clamp, invert, threshold_hysteresis, slew_limit, lowpass, gate, piecewise_table) so the graph reads the same whichever side evaluates it; the editor labels each edge with where it runs and why. Placeable on the home as a module (control contract); edit mode only; safety interlock mirrors the hub's (pause and estop disarm client-side mappings too). Depends on RFC-078 and RFC-067 landing for the hub half; the client half can start against the buttplug toys modules that landed 2026-10-01.

title: RFC-088: Flip, a rail-bound direction flip: home swaps ends, one toggle on the rail's control row, refused while a source owns the rail
description: Operator direction 2026-10-01 while running the RFC queue: the machine calls one end home; a single control inverts the machine so the other end is home, useful on a hardware that can be mounted either way. Draft RFC-088: (1) a stored mode, inverted, on the machine-modes STATE channel (0x1030) written through its writer, persisted across reboot (it describes how the machine is mounted), with a registered role (proposed axis.inverted) so a client binds it by identity. (2) Effect: position 0 becomes the far end; the hub mirrors position telemetry, the travel window (window.* roles) and every c2h stream and intent target, so no client needs to know the state to behave; presets keep their meaning. (3) Gate (hub MUST): NACK SOURCE_CONFLICT while any source owns the rail (only between streams), NACK while unhomed; it never acts mid-motion. (4) RENDERING: one toggle control with two states on the rail's control row beside home and override/return (RFC-085), an essential binding of the axis archetype where the role is present, confirm-gated on every class (reversing a rail under a person is a real act), label Invert (operator may prefer Flip; decide at landing). (5) Nucleus follow-up: the mode, the mirroring in the kinetic and telemetry paths, a bench stamp that a homed rail flips and telemetry reads travel minus position.

title: RFC-086: Units: add deg, us and a hub-time stamp unit; display autoranging is a client choice
description: Operator ruling 2026-10-01 while running the RFC queue. Draft RFC-086 in RFC-QUEUE.md: (1) unit_ids gains deg (angle; radians are a math convenience, not a knob unit), us (microseconds; hub time is microseconds everywhere in section 7 and only ms and s are registered) and hub_s (seconds in the hub's own section 7.1 timebase, distinct from s so a client knows to apply its CLOCK offset; this is the unit the RFC-083 datetime.* roles carry). (2) RENDERING gains one sentence: a client MAY autorange SI prefixes for DISPLAY (85 mV for a V field reading 0.085) and MUST NOT alter the wire unit or scale; magnitude lives in the field's scale, never in a prefix, so no prefix or range vocabulary exists. title: RFC-079: Config mode and the setup category
description: Drafted 2026-09-26 in spec/RFC-QUEUE.md. Origin: operator rulings 2026-09-26, Isotope/provisioning. The window's single grant is configure in config mode (12.3 grant rule amended for this gesture). New ui_categories 15 setup holding the RFC-069 provisioning intent, the identity.name setting (RFC-016/026) and the RFC-076 accessory-admin control; clients render it generically, wizard pattern (RENDERING 10) recommended, never a hub-specific screen. CANON FLAG noted: hardware/flagship/SPEC.md says PAIR held at power-on = AP config mode, contradicting the no-softAP ruling; the hardware repo must resolve it. comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RULING 2026-10-01 (operator), scope of category 15 setup: it is the machine COMMISSIONING surface, not only first-run network. A hub places there every writable configuration the machine exposes that a person needs to make the Flagship usable: network credentials, machine name, accessory pairing, AND the machine's own geometry and ceilings (rail length, travel window, speed ceiling, accel ceiling, jerk ceiling, geometry, degree-to-mm ratio and the like). Pinout and board-level facts stay out (TBD, not catalog). Categories are static per entry, so these entries carry setup in every mode. Nucleus follow-up: machine-config (0x1000) and the kinetic ceilings move to category setup; the wizard steps through them in authoring order. RFC-054 is OBSOLETE (see its own bead): no hub-discloses-credentials path; embedded clients and Isotope accessories are ESP-NOW only unless provisionable on their own.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Operator principle 2026-10-01, recorded for the setup category and for Nucleus doctrine: the Flagship hardware is a motor controller that can be strapped to any machine with a motor. How motor motion translates to the machine's motion (linear travel, degree-to-mm ratio, rail length, geometry, ceilings) is the OWNER'S configuration responsibility, entered through the setup category, never firmware knowledge. The catalog describes a motor plus configured geometry; the rail archetype is the presentation of that configuration, not an assumption in the firmware. Nucleus follow-up: machine geometry and the kinetic ceilings are setup-category settings with sane defaults and a required first-run pass, not compile-time constants.

title: RFC-078: Accessory conformance profile and the hub relationship engine
description: Drafted 2026-09-26 in spec/RFC-QUEUE.md. Origin: operator rulings 2026-09-26, Isotope. title: Spec gap: §5.4 gives no lead cap or semantics for future-anchored samples-kind STREAM points (Nucleus clamps 250 ms and treats the anchor as a scheduled start)
description: Found 2026-09-25 by Phosphor ph-vdk.26. SPEC §5.4 says a samples timestamp is the instant the sample describes but sets no maximum lead for samples-kind streams and does not say whether a future anchor is a deadline (arrive by) or a scheduled start. Nucleus kinetic.hpp commit() clamps to 250 ms and treats it as a start, so a client-side duration lead delays the chase instead of setting a deadline; measured +5.5% overshoot on a 1 Hz sine at ~30 ms send jitter. Needs an RFC clause: lead cap named in the registry (max_future_schedule_ms already exists for segments?) and the anchor semantics for samples. Cross-ref RFC-058, RFC-071.

Arrival semantics for c2h samples timestamps (reading 5.4's 'instant the sample describes'); max_future_schedule_ms cap widened to every c2h STREAM (matches Nucleus kStreamFarFutureUs 250 ms clamp). title: JS client: blob chunks for ns != 0 are dropped; no store blob request API
description: clients/js/session.js handleBlobChunk (line 688) hardcodes single-namespace operation: line 694 'if (h.ns !== 0) return;' with comment (691-693) 'This session transfers exactly one namespace: the catalog. A store chunk belongs to that fetch's own reassembler; dropping it here is what keeps the two from corrupting each other.' There IS no second reassembler: the module has exactly one BlobReassembler instance (blob), built and reset only by requestCatalog() (line 583). The public API returned at line 1428 exposes requestCatalog but no store-blob equivalent (no requestStoreBlob/fetchStoreItem), and sendBlobDone (line 632) is only ever invoked from the catalog path (pumpBlobRepair, refuseBlob). Net effect: SPEC 8.7 STORE items (ns=1, blob_namespaces.store) are completely unreadable from this reference client -- any BLOB_CHUNK a hub sends for a store transfer is silently discarded at line 694, and there is no way to originate one, since nothing calls BLOB_REQ with ns=1.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RULING 2026-10-01 (operator): RFC-066 ACCEPTED AS AMENDED. Retitle to modulators. Term is 'modulator', role family mod.* on the modulator's fields: mod.amount, mod.rise, mod.hold, mod.fall, mod.rest, mod.phase, plus optional mod.shape (select; absent = the cycling trapezoid). Field unit carries the clock (strokes or seconds); roles bake in no time base. 'Lane' is retired as a term.

SPEC §18-24 item 24 still ends "Still not shipped: the hub does not abort
a sustained-congestion transfer with NACK BUSY, and no reference client or
hub emits BLOB_DONE" -- now false. registry.yaml's frame_types 0x20 note
still ends "Implementation: Phase D (post-batch hub work)". Both are
normative surfaces and need an RFC-gated edit.

DEVIATION WORTH A RULING: §8.4 row 4 keys the abort on the §10.3
congestion signal being sustained. The implementation keys it on LACK OF
PROGRESS instead (no chunk emitted for 5 s, whether from the in-flight
budget or a transport refusal). Reason: a binding whose adapter never

title: RFC-037: catalog key 18 size not emitted by reference encoder
description: Registered, decodable, specified; needs one deliberate encoder pass plus a declared==derived conformance check.
notes:
2026-09-03 -- BLOCKED ON A RULING (C-6). Measured, not implemented.

Emitting key 18 unconditionally MOVES THE TWO FROZEN CATALOG PINS.
Measured by temporarily patching encodeLayoutField() to emit
`w.key(18).uintVal(f.wireSize())` for every layout field, encoding
conformance::miniCatalog(), then reverting (tree verified clean):

  catalog_encoded_bytes  775  ->  805   (+30 = 2 B x 15 layout fields)
  catalog_etag           F4A28FBB58CED16A  ->  8C5D68F41AD0325E

Both are pinned at spec/vectors/manifest.yaml:21-22 under
"FROZEN AT THE v1.0 TAG (K-01 and K-02 pins). Changing the fixture moves
both and is a protocol break, not a refactor -- SPEC §17.2", and asserted
at test/native/test_slopsync_catalog/test_main.cpp:136,199,244. That
file's own M2b banner (line ~447) states the invariant this would break
verbatim: "If either pin ever shifts, something optional was made
mandatory." Key 18 is `? 18 => uint` in spec/schema/catalog.cddl -- making
it unconditional is exactly that.

The two frozen-hash artifacts are NOT touched by an encoder change and
their hashes are unchanged:
  lib/slopsync/include/slopsync/conformance/mini_catalog.hpp
    2a90bf8a5658b4ecb2c96a28d9aa9e39a908926c91e0aebba5844366c3252eb2
  spec/vectors/fixtures/mini-catalog.yaml
    b2b6a3063e66b56916683c6878ce237085fbcd8ea145c02369f5b96a45c6901c

RULING NEEDED, three shapes:
 (a) Always emit, re-freeze K-01/K-02 to 805 / 8C5D68F41AD0325E. Pre-tag,
     so a legal break -- but it is a break, and it is what RFC-037's own
     "one deliberate encoder pass" text asks for.
 (b) Author-opt-in `size` on LayoutField, emitted only when set. Pins
     unmoved, key 18 becomes exercisable, and RFC-037's "add an emitting
     fixture" obligation is satisfied by a test-local fixture rather than
     by the frozen one. Costs a has-flag the ruling may later delete.
 (c) Defer to the v1.1 fixture pass, which manifest.yaml line 95 already
     names as the place other pin-moving fixture work was parked.

Nothing was changed in the tree for this item. Blocks on the ruling; the
declared==derived conformance check has nothing to check until then.

title: rfc-gate hook does not fire on scripted writes to SPEC.md / registry.yaml; add a pre-commit path check
description:
The RFC gate (.claude/hooks/rfc-gate.sh) is a Claude Code PreToolUse hook matched on Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit. A Bash-driven write (python/sed/heredoc) to spec/SPEC.md or spec/registry/registry.yaml never passes through it, and git commit does not re-check. The 2026-10-01 queue landing wrote both files that way and so bypassed the gate incidentally (the RFCs were accepted, so no harm this time; the gate simply was not consulted).

Proposed fix (not implemented; hooks are operator-owned): a git pre-commit check that, when the staged paths include spec/SPEC.md or spec/registry/registry.yaml, requires an accepted-family RFC reference using the same lookup rfc-gate.sh does (branch rfc-NNN or .claude/.rfc-ticket, status Accepted/Landed in spec/RFC-QUEUE.md) and otherwise refuses the commit. One shared script both hooks call keeps the rule in one home. A commit-msg variant could take the RFC id from the subject line instead of the branch.

Two adjacent observations: (1) git core.hooksPath here is C:\Users\Atlan\Documents\SlopSync\.beads\hooks, which no longer exists after the rename, so no git hook in this repo runs today (beads' own pre-commit included); a pre-commit gate needs that repointed first. (2) The branch-name lookup is coarse: on feat/rfc-050-blob-done every SPEC/registry edit passes as RFC-050 regardless of which RFC it lands.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: c8c2c2d: tools/rfc-gate-check.sh (POSIX sh, git/grep/awk, no python) called from .beads/hooks/pre-commit after the beads block; refuses a commit whose staged paths include spec/SPEC.md or spec/registry/registry.yaml unless the rfc-gate lookup (branch rfc-NNN, else .claude/.rfc-ticket) finds an Accepted/Landed RFC. Honors GIT_INDEX_FILE (path-limited and private-index commits). core.hooksPath already points at this repo's .beads/hooks (observation 1 resolved). 8 cases verified in a scratch clone. NOT DONE (operator's call): .claude/hooks/rfc-gate.sh still has its own copy of the lookup; it gates the agent's own edits, so an agent did not rewire it. Observation 2 (coarse branch lookup) unchanged: on feat/rfc-050-blob-done every normative commit passes as RFC-050.
